A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLAIMDB. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding tables, figures, methods, and prompts can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 30 models, private-test results in Table 3, and validation of its LLM judge panel against human annotations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original 30-model public evaluation and adds a tool-free control, SQL-query error analysis, and database token measurements.

M1.justification: The SQL filtering rules, GPT-5 claim generation, judge panel, similarity-based NEI sampling, and principal SQL-agent procedure are retained. The generation and judging prompts match across versions; new SQL/AST examples illustrate existing rules.

E1.justification: Both retain 53,368 claims from the same 80 databases, with unchanged domains, labels, and NEI categories. Section 5 still defines public and private test splits. The tool-free control tests the existing task; removal of private-test scores does not establish removal of that dataset.

E2.justification: The public comparison retains all 30 model backbones; nemotron-3-nano:30b is a clarified name. V2 adds one comparison configuration, GPT-5-mini without tools, in Section 6.3. The separate private-test comparison is no longer reported.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a tools-disabled GPT-5-mini control and categorizes SQL-query outcomes. Appendix A adds CSV-based token measurement and claim-weighted summaries. Existing test sizes, classification metrics, and the 20-tool-call limit remain unchanged; newly disclosed decoding details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens supporting validation: the tool-free control probes parametric shortcuts, Figure 7 analyzes query failures and their relationship to prediction correctness, and Appendix A measures database context sizes. V1 lacks these analyses. The human-judge comparison chart is removed, although its aggregate recall finding remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed performance estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The formatting-error retry policy is unchanged. Specifying four problematic human-annotated cases clarifies the existing recall result without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All public classification values in Table 2 remain identical. However, v2 removes the 27-model private-test table and token/cost results. It adds tool-free GPT-5-mini results (0.367 accuracy, 0.253 macro-F1), SQL success rates of 93% and 99% for GPT-5-mini and Claude Haiku 4.5, and token-size measurements. Reported tool-call distributions also change: GPT-4o-mini's mean falls from 8.2 to 5.2 in v1 Figure 11 versus v2 Figure 12, without an explanation.

T1.justification: The AST inclusion criteria and macro-F1 definition are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations appear; the added SQL examples and token-size discussion are explanatory and empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the explicit first-benchmark claim and the statement that no model exceeds 83% accuracy. V2 adds the approximately 110M-token context summary while retaining the central contributions concerning large structured evidence, model difficulty, and abstention failures.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the tool-free control as evidence against solving CLAIMDB through parametric knowledge alone, and successful SQL execution as evidence of deeper reasoning failures. It explains why token estimates are conservative but removes the cost-performance discussion. The principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents CSV concatenation and the GPT-5 tokenizer, specifies medium reasoning for NEI generation, and states that NEI similarity scores are released. Its Ministral 3 rows replace unspecified topK/topP entries with 50/90 as printed. These are additional disclosures; token-usage and dollar-cost details are removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds work on synthetic claim generation and scientific, legal, and multimodal verification. It acknowledges Devasier et al. (2025, 2026), distinguishing CLAIMDB from pilot-scale or single-table large-data work. Additional citations support the contamination discussion and recursive language models.

P1.justification: The section framework and most existing prose and prompts persist. V2 revises the abstract and selected explanations, adds an introductory roadmap, reorders discussion paragraphs, expands acknowledgments, and reorganizes appendices around the added material.

P2.justification: V2 adds SQL-outcome and database-token charts plus four SQL/AST diagrams. It removes v1's human-judge bar chart and private-results table, drops Table 2's token column, and adds accuracy annotations to the revised tool-call histograms. These substantially change the visual evidence and explanatory displays.

improvement.justification: The new tool-free and SQL-error analyses probe shortcut solving and failure sources that v1 left untested. Token-count instructions, filtering examples, and disclosure that judge recall rests on four problematic cases improve auditability. These modest gains are partly offset by removal of private-test and token/cost evidence; the core method and public classification results remain unchanged.
